final_rationale: The verdict changes toward noncompliance, but not because of new evidence. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position by conceding the key points: the Spanish-language billing support segment is still exposed, no approved risk acceptance covers that exposure, and rollout controls do not themselves satisfy the policy condition. On the available record, that narrower framing does not reach compliant_with_caveats. A caveated result would require evidence that the governing policy permits certification with an unresolved exposed limitation based on disclosure alone, and that the required disclosure is actually present in the certification artifact. The admissible record instead includes policy text stating that rollout controls and monitoring mitigate the weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists. Because neither predicate is satisfied, the certification position is not merely weakly supported; it is inconsistent with the stated policy condition.
remaining_concerns: The Spanish-language billing support segment remains below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No reviewed and approved risk-acceptance record is in the admissible record for that exact exposure.
The stated policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate this weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists.
No admissible evidence shows the certification policy allows launch solely on the basis of disclosure when the affected segment remains exposed.
No admissible artifact was provided showing the actual model-card disclosure in the certification record, even if disclosure alone were relevant.
